title: Antipsychotic medication for psychosis
description: Antipsychotic medication is the main treatment for psychosis, and the striatum, deep in the brain, is its main target. One study scanned people at rest during a first episode of psychosis, before and after 12 weeks of treatment. Across the group, one link strengthened: between the right ventral striatum and the left thalamus. The people whose psychosis improved most also showed the largest strengthening of links between the striatum and the front of the brain, the hippocampus and the insula; that is a relationship across people and is described, not drawn. The line shows the change in how closely two areas work together since before treatment: pulsing means more.
caveat: All findings come from one study of 24 people in a first episode of psychosis, treated with risperidone or aripiprazole, and 24 people without psychosis scanned twice. Only one link changed across the whole group; the other findings link the size of the change in each person to how much their psychosis improved. Before treatment, the striatum's links did not differ significantly from people without psychosis. The right ventral striatum is drawn as the right caudate, an approximation. These are averages across groups of people, not a picture of any one person's brain. Treatments help many people, not everyone, and in different ways. This is not medical advice: talk to a doctor or therapist about what is right for you.

phases.caption: Early in a first episode of psychosis. In this study the striatum's links did not differ from people without psychosis, so the brain is drawn at rest.

phases.name: Twelve weeks of medication
phases.caption: Daily antipsychotic medication. People were not scanned during this time.

citations.title: Antipsychotic treatment and functional connectivity of the striatum in first-episode schizophrenia.
citations.quote: Patients were scanned at baseline and after 12 weeks of treatment with either risperidone or aripiprazole.

phases.name: What changed
phases.caption: After twelve weeks, the right ventral striatum works more closely with the left thalamus. In the people whose psychosis improved most, the striatum also came to work more closely with the anterior cingulate, the dorsolateral prefrontal cortex, the hippocampus and the anterior insula, and less closely with parietal areas.

phases.name: What stayed the same
phases.caption: Most of the striatum's links did not change across the group as a whole; the changes tracked how much each person improved. Side effects and longer-term changes were not part of this study.

order.rationale: This last part is a summary of what the studies did not find or did not measure, not a later point in time.

connections.explanation: The right ventral striatum worked more closely with the left thalamus after 12 weeks of antipsychotic treatment, the only link that changed across the whole group, in one study of 24 people. Drawn from the right caudate, an approximation. The other striatal links changed in proportion to how much psychosis improved, a relationship across people that is described but not drawn.
